newsitem.title: USA: Austria says to put up 417 mln SDRs for IMF's NAB.
newsitem.headline: Austria says to put up 417 mln SDRs for IMF's NAB.

text.p: Austria, one of 13 nations which has agreed to contribute to a new stand-by fund for the International Monetary Fund, said on Monday it would contribute 417 million Special Drawing Rights to the facility.

The new fund, called the New Arrangements to Borrow, will exist alongside the former General Arrangements to Borrow made available to the IMF by the Group of 10 countries. The new NAB will double the size of the old GAB to 34 billion SDRs.
The Special Drawing Right, the IMF's own currency, is worth about $1.44 at current exchange rates.
"We have agreed to put 417 million SDRs into NAB," Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima told a briefing on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank annual meetings.
He said the funds were only a stand-by facility, designed to offer the Fund access to extra cash in emergencies.
Klima welcomed the decision to set up the parallel NAB in a way which will allow participating countries some say in how and when the funds are used.

The G10 -- which groups Belgium, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the United States -- had originally resisted the idea of new countries being involved in such decisions as they did not want to foster a broad expansion of the 11-nation G10 group.
